name: Pipe Flow Calculator
description: Calculate volumetric flow rate in a pipe from pipe diameter and fluid velocity using Q = A × v.

seo.title: Pipe Flow Calculator - Free Online Engineering Tool
seo.description: Calculate pipe flow rate from diameter and velocity — Continuity equation Q = πd²/4 × v with unit conversion

formula.explanation: Continuity equation: Q = A × v × 3600 where A = πd²/4. With d in meters and v in m/s, Q is in m³/h (×3600 converts seconds to hours).

content.introduction: Calculate volumetric flow rate through a pipe given its inner diameter and the fluid velocity. This is the fundamental continuity equation used in pipe sizing and hydraulic design.

example.description: A 100mm ID pipe with water flowing at 2 m/s carries approximately 56.55 m³/h.

faq.q: What is a typical pipe velocity for water?
faq.a: Typical water velocity in pipes is 1-3 m/s. Values above 3 m/s may cause erosion and high pressure drop.
Q = π × d² / 4 × v × 3600 (continuity equation, converted to m³/h). This assumes the pipe is flowing full.

faq.q: How do I convert m3/h to L/s?
faq.a: Divide m3/h by 3.6. For example, 56.55 m3/h = 15.7 L/s. To convert L/s to m3/h, multiply by 3.6.

faq.q: How do I convert m3/h to US gpm?
faq.a: Multiply m3/h by 4.403. For example, 56.55 m3/h = 249 US gpm. Conversely divide gpm by 4.403 to get m3/h.

faq.q: What is the flow rate of a 50mm pipe at 1 m/s?
faq.a: Q = pi x 0.05^2 / 4 x 1 x 3600 = 7.07 m3/h (1.96 L/s). At 2 m/s the same pipe carries 14.1 m3/h.

faq.q: How do I calculate pipe diameter from flow rate?
faq.a: Rearrange the continuity equation: d = sqrt(4Q / (pi x v)). Use consistent units - with Q in m3/s and v in m/s, d is in meters. Then select the nearest standard pipe size.

sections.heading: Typical Design Velocities by Service
sections.body:
Recommended design velocities for common services:
Pump suction (water): 0.6-1.5 m/s | Pump discharge (water): 1.5-3.0 m/s | General water lines: 1-3 m/s | Boiler feed water: 1.5-4.5 m/s | Oil (viscous): 0.3-1.5 m/s | Steam (low pressure): 20-40 m/s | Compressed air: 6-15 m/s | Gas (natural): 10-30 m/s.
Velocities above 3 m/s for water increase erosion and pressure drop; above 4.5 m/s erosion-corrosion risk rises sharply.

sections.heading: Worked Example: Sizing a Water Line
sections.body:
A pump must deliver 30 m3/h of water. Select a pipe diameter for a design velocity of 2 m/s.
Step 1 - required area: A = Q / v = (30/3600) / 2 = 4.167 x 10^-3 m2.
Step 2 - required diameter: d = sqrt(4A/pi) = sqrt(4 x 4.167 x 10^-3 / pi) = 0.0728 m = 72.8 mm.
Step 3 - select standard pipe: use 80 mm nominal bore (ID ~80 mm).
Check: Q = pi x 0.08^2/4 x 2 x 3600 = 36.2 m3/h, velocity at 30 m3/h = 1.66 m/s - within the 1-3 m/s range.

sections.heading: Unit Conversion Guide
sections.body:
Flow rate: 1 m3/h = 0.2778 L/s = 4.403 US gpm = 3.667 UK gpm.
1 L/s = 3.6 m3/h = 15.85 US gpm. 1 US gpm = 0.2271 m3/h.
Velocity: 1 m/s = 3.281 ft/s. Diameter: 1 mm = 0.03937 in.
Example: 56.55 m3/h = 56.55 x 4.403 = 249 US gpm.
